clue.text: In essence, a nasty threat

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted or turned bad, so the letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: part of the anagram fodder
the rest of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone reduces a menacing message to its core: basically, it's a nasty threat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom at heart means fundamentally, deep down, which is what 'in essence' says.

clue.text: One adult missing from Handel opera in US city

indicators.note: when something is missing from a title, that title is left one letter short

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
Atalanta is an opera Handel wrote in 1736

explanation.surface: A performance of a Handel opera in an American city is short one grown-up singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one of the A's out of ATALANTA (the second one) to leave ATLANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the state capital of Georgia, a major city in the United States.

clue.text: Physically fit, but callous

blocks.note: first meaning: tough and in rugged physical condition
second meaning: unfeeling, showing no sympathy

explanation.surface: A character sketch: someone in great shape physically, but heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone tough both in body and in temperament, so it covers fitness and hard-heartedness alike.

clue.text: Collect a lot

blocks.note: taken as written
a mass is a large quantity, a lot

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a lot' as two pieces: the article A and a word for a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate things, the same as to collect them.

clue.text: Pub with a small restaurant

blocks.note: a tavern is an inn or pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub that has a little eatery attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating place, a modest restaurant.

clue.text: Composer in taxi going back to hospital

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from its end
'to' means added onto, so one piece is attached to the next

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A composer is driven back to hospital by taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach was the great German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Bishop's account tainted such a god

indicators.note: tainted means spoiled or corrupted, so the word's letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
AC is the abbreviation for account
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bishop's version of events has been corrupted by talk of a pagan deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop's' is Bishop has: B followed by AC, then the jumbled letters of 'such'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine, so he is a god.

clue.text: Wounded girls with swords

blocks.note: cut means wounded by a blade
lasses is a Scottish and northern word for girls

explanation.surface: A grim scene of girls hurt by blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, once used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: My daughter's to advise public prosecutor

blocks.note: Lor! is an old exclamation of surprise, like My!
D is the abbreviation for daughter
to advocate is to recommend or urge, to advise

explanation.surface: A parent explains that their daughter's job is giving advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation, as in 'My!' or 'Lor!'; 's is short for has.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Advocate is Scotland's chief law officer, who heads public prosecution there.

clue.text: Tart in trousers half off

indicators.note: half off means one half of the word is removed, leaving the front part

blocks.note: flannels are trousers made of flannel, worn for cricket

explanation.surface: A floozy whose trousers are half falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' wants to be a person; it is the pastry. Flannels are white trousers worn for cricket and tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, a kind of tart.

clue.text: Approaches some within earshot

indicators.note: 'some' means only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Something comes close enough for a few people to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nears is a verb meaning comes closer to, the same as approaches.

clue.text: Tries during proper drill

indicators.note: during means happening within, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: real means genuine, proper
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: Attempts made in the middle of a proper training exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, but here it is the courtroom sense: a judge tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run, and a drill is likewise a practice exercise.

clue.text: Rugby player is hard and aloof

blocks.note: a stand-off is the rugby position also called fly-half
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rugby player described as tough and distant.
explanation.walkthrough: The stand-off, or fly-half, is the back who usually directs play in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Standoffish describes someone cool and distant in manner, which is what aloof means.

clue.text: Names I confused after onset of awful medical condition

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter is used
confused means mixed up, so the letters come in a jumbled order
'after' means placed behind, so the jumbled part follows the other piece

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps muddling names fears an awful illness is setting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia, loss of memory, is a recognised medical disorder.

clue.text: Shell out about fifty on our show

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round a letter
in a down clue 'on' means placed above, so one piece comes before the other

blocks.note: to shell out is to spend money
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paying about fifty pounds for a performance of our own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a performance of our own, but it means grand display; 'on' places the second piece after the first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour means magnificent display, as does show in the sense of pomp or spectacle.

clue.text: Spot inhabited by American bear

indicators.note: a place inhabited by someone has them living inside it

blocks.note: a stain is a spot or mark
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A location where an American bear lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal living in the spot, but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to bear its weight or hold it up.

clue.text: One of three allowed to go on outing

indicators.note: 'to go on' means placed after, so one piece is attached to the end of the other

blocks.note: a trip is an excursion, an outing
let means allowed

explanation.surface: One of three children gets permission to go on a day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at the same birth.

clue.text: Before end of encounter, draw level

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is used
'Before' says one piece is placed ahead of the other in the answer

blocks.note: a tie is a drawn game
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sports match is drawn level just before it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the last letter first, but 'Before' puts the draw in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as in tiers of seating or a tiered cake.

clue.text: Keen, a number carrying spades

indicators.note: something carrying a thing holds it within, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: thirty is a number
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic gardener counts the spades they are carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty can mean eager or craving, as in thirsty for knowledge, so keen.

clue.text: English breaking records as well

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one letter goes in

blocks.note: B-sides are the second tracks on singles records
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English athlete breaking records, and more on top of that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking records' suggests sporting feats; the records are vinyl B-sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides is an adverb meaning in addition or also, the same as as well.

clue.text: Ring party, or page?

blocks.note: a bell is something you ring, giving a ring
a hop is an informal dance or party

explanation.surface: A choice of whether to phone a party or send a message on a pager.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop is a hotel page, a uniformed boy who carries luggage and runs errands.

clue.text: One expected to score in match?

definitions.text: One expected to score in match?

blocks.clueFragment: One expected to score in match?
blocks.note: surface reading: a forward whose job is scoring goals in a football game
setter's reading: one who scratches a matchstick to light it, scoring its head

explanation.walkthrough: The football reading is the obvious one; the question mark hints at the second sense of striking a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker is the attacking forward in football and also anything that strikes, such as a person lighting a match.

clue.text: Key German city — lecture mostly about one

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round a letter

blocks.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
a talk is a lecture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A key talk in a German city, roughly about one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: TALK loses its last letter to become TAL, which then wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial or vital, which is what essential means.

clue.text: Dogsbody, good for running round Egypt's capital

indicators.note: running suggests something in motion, out of place, so the letters are mixed
a word's capital is its leading letter, so only the first is taken
round means surrounding, so the mixed letters go about another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the anagram fodder
the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A lowly assistant, useful for running errands round Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egypt's capital' reads as Cairo, but it means the first letter of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer is someone who runs errands, a menial helper, as is a dogsbody.

clue.text: Verbally attacked kid nicking piece of tiling

indicators.note: a piece of the word here is just its opening letter
nicking means stealing, so the stolen letter is taken inside

blocks.note: a kid is a young goat; here the animal itself
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A child who stole a tile got a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child, but stands for a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got at is to be criticised or nagged, so verbally attacked.

clue.text: Achieves the required result as a conjuror?

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for succeeding or working
second meaning, literal and whimsical: what a magician does on stage

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a playful literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means works or is effective, and a conjuror literally performs a trick.

clue.text: Play about king in ancient city

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds a letter

blocks.note: to toy is to play
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A drama about a monarch set in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the city of Greek legend besieged in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Baseball player in jug

blocks.note: first meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter
second meaning: a large jug for pouring

explanation.surface: A baseball player locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In jug' suggests in prison (jug is slang for jail); here jug is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is both the baseball player who throws and a large jug with a lip for pouring.
